subject: science
domain: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes
skillName: Cells as the Unit of Life
intro: A cell is the smallest unit of a living thing that can carry out life processes. Cell theory has three main ideas: all living things are made of one or more cells, the cell is the basic unit of structure and function in living things, and all cells come from existing cells. Organisms made of a single cell are called unicellular (such as bacteria and amoebas); organisms made of many cells are called multicellular (such as plants and animals).

items.prompt: A scientist looks at pond water under a microscope and sees tiny organisms, each made of just one cell that moves and feeds on its own. Are these organisms living, and are they unicellular or multicellular?

steps: Cell theory says all living things are made of cells, and these organisms are made of cells.
Each organism carries out life processes (moving, feeding) on its own.
Because each organism is made of only one cell, it is unicellular.

items.prompt: Why can we say that a human and a bacterium are both alive even though a human has trillions of cells and a bacterium has only one?

steps: Cell theory states that all living things are made of one or more cells.
A bacterium meets this with a single cell; a human meets it with many cells.
The number of cells does not decide whether something is alive, only that it is built from cells that carry out life functions.
solution.answer: Both are made of cells, so both are living things.

items.prompt: A student claims a new cell can simply appear from nonliving material. How does cell theory respond to this claim?

steps: Cell theory states that all cells come from existing cells.
New cells form when existing cells divide, not from nonliving material.
So the claim contradicts cell theory.
solution.answer: The claim is incorrect; cells come only from other cells.

items.prompt: Name the three main ideas of cell theory.

steps: Idea 1: all living things are made of one or more cells.
Idea 2: the cell is the basic unit of structure and function.
Idea 3: all cells come from existing cells.
solution.answer: All living things are made of cells; the cell is the basic unit of life; all cells come from existing cells.

items.prompt: An amoeba is made of a single cell. Is it unicellular or multicellular? Is it alive?

steps: Made of one cell means unicellular.
It carries out life processes, so it is alive.

items.prompt: A maple tree is made of many different kinds of cells. What word describes an organism made of many cells?

steps: An organism made of many cells is multicellular.
